title: De ahí que + subjuntivo: sacar una conclusión

sections.content: De ahí que (hence, which is why) draws a conclusion from everything just said, and always takes the subjunctive in the clause that follows -- a formal, essay-style connector perfectly suited to a closing synthesis pulling several lessons' worth of evidence into one verdict. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: La crisis expuso brutalmente la vulnerabilidad del modelo exportador. De ahí que muchos historiadores consideren 1929 uno de los verdaderos puntos de inflexión.
items.english: The crisis brutally exposed the export model's vulnerability. Hence many historians consider 1929 one of the true turning points.

items.spanish: La crisis demostró que ese modelo ya no bastaba. De ahí que resultara tan difícil, después de 1929, defender seriamente su continuidad.
items.english: The crisis showed that model was no longer enough. That's why it became so difficult, after 1929, to seriously defend its continuation.

items.spanish: Se abrió un espacio político para nuevas ideas. De ahí que surgieran figuras políticas de un tipo nuevo, capaces de apelar directamente a las masas.
items.english: A political space opened up for new ideas. Hence new-style political figures emerged, capable of appealing directly to the masses.

items.spanish: La industrialización comenzó casi por necesidad. De ahí que se convirtiera, en las siguientes décadas, en la política económica dominante de la región.
items.english: Industrialization began almost out of necessity. That's why it became, in the following decades, the region's dominant economic policy.

sections.content: De ahí que sits between two ideas as a bridge, not at the very start of a paragraph's first sentence -- it always follows the evidence it's drawing a conclusion from, as every example above shows.
